{"sha":"a2af14d9d715d586852e56428cb2f7f0fdcc5156","html_url":"https://github.com/AI-Riksarkivet/rask/commit/a2af14d9d715d586852e56428cb2f7f0fdcc5156","commit":{"author":{"name":"Borg93","email":"Borg93@users.noreply.github.com","date":"2026-10-22T11:20:13Z"},"committer":{"name":"Borg93","email":"Borg93@users.noreply.github.com","date":"2026-10-22T11:20:13Z"},"message":"feat(catalog,lineage,notifications,maintenance): LH-524 — FGA objects are table:<uuid> and namespace:<uuid>, so a rename moves no grant (ADR 0173 §8)

No name reaches OpenFGA. Every table and namespace object is the uuid the catalog minted
(`fga.table_object`, `fga.namespace_object`, `fga.object_of`), parent and child edges join uuids,
and a top-level namespace still hangs off its warehouse. Every door stays addressed by name.

- catalog: `dependencies.Resolver` (`ResolverDep`) resolves each name once per request, shared by
  `authorize`, the tier judge and `ResolvedTableDep`. `authorize` asks the resolved uuid object; an
  absent name is refused 403 and audited by name, and only a read door converts it to 404 for a
  reader of the parent. Every refusal names the object by its name, never its uuid. Undrop and tasks
  resolve a trashed name through the uuid its trash record keeps.
- catalog: create, declare, register, the namespace doors and the provenance boot seed owner and
  edges on the minted uuid (`seed_ownership(..., uuid=...)`); `created` and the stale-on-create
  revoke go, since a re-created name is another uuid. `fga.parent_object` and `move_ownership` go:
  a rename writes no tuple, and into another namespace it moves only the parent edge
  (`move_parent_edge`).
- catalog: every listing batch-checks its own candidates and fills its page
  (`fga_deps.authorized_page`, LH-223 #145); `authorization_truncated` and X-Authorization-Truncated
  go. Projects, warehouses, bindings and models batch-check their records. Only /management/v1/me
  and the admin's raw ListObjects explorer call list_objects.
- catalog: grant, review, access and graph answers carry `name` beside the uuid `object`. Control
  events name the uuid in `object_id` with the name in new `object_name`; the binding-cache eviction
  reads `object_name`. Holds, due records and erasure obligations are checked on the uuid they record.
- catalog: the cascade walk ends the records of an object found only by its edge (the edge names its
  uuid); a warehouse delete revokes trashed objects by the uuid their record keeps and ends a
  namespace an earlier attempt left by the warehouse's child edge.
- lineage: every check asks `table:<uuid>` from the dataset's `lance` facet (`governed_refs`,
  `output_refs`); the HTTP door stamps resolved uuids before its gate; outputs are never exempt, and an
  output naming no table is refused as ungoverned. The rename-register carve-out goes. Reads,
  the DLQ and the derived walk govern on recorded uuids; LINEAGE_FGA_OBJECT_TYPE goes.
- notifications: pointers hold `table:<uuid>` with `object_name`; an output with no uuid is
  undeliverable; the inbox control-lane test is narrowed to non-table objects.
- maintenance: the purge revokes the trashed object's uuid and refuses when it cannot read it; drift
  detection compares the store's table objects with the uuids the claims and the trash hold.
- seed_estate resolves each table and namespace grant to its uuid through Describe; git holds names.
- docs, skills (rask-lance-catalog, rask-notifications, openfga), e2e acceptance modules, OpenAPI and
  generated types.

Stated bounds:
- Decision-door answers are keyed by the uuid object and carry no name: no uuid-to-name reverse lookup.
- A registry model keeps `table:models$<name>`: it is no lance-namespace table and has no uuid.
- A Skip drop over an absent namespace answers 403 (destructive door, no existence oracle); its
  leftover binding is repaired by the warehouse unbind door. Drift detection has no namespace ghost
  category.
- Read and data doors still call the backend by name after authorizing the uuid (authorize-then-act).
- A service-account producer posting lineage over HTTP cannot resolve names and is refused; none
  exists in the estate today.
- viewer/search (`service_kit/media/authz.py`) and the annotator still check table:<name>, and fail
  closed. The materialized-view seed goes (no backend creates a view).
- A listing costs one describe and one claim read per candidate it judges.
- The live rebuild and read-back (ADR 0173 §12) follow this commit.

Tests, one per closes-when clause, each red with its line broken in a snapshot worktree or red
before the fix:
- rename keeps the grant and writes no tuple; a re-created name is refused; every created tuple names
  a uuid; `sp ace` creates and describes:
  services/catalog/tests/test_a_grant_is_held_by_the_objects_uuid.py (red before the fix).
- past 1,000 objects, paging, sibling namespaces:
  services/catalog/tests/test_a_listing_judges_its_own_candidates.py (replaces the two unit listing files).
- catalog write and outside producer pass lineage and the watcher's bell rings after a rename:
  tests/integration/test_a_renamed_table_keeps_its_lineage_checks_and_its_watchers_bell.py.
- the bus door admits a write naming a name a rename took:
  services/lineage/tests/test_the_bus_door_authorizes_what_it_records.py.
- no ghost on a healthy estate with a renamed table:
  tests/integration/test_drift_repair_keeps_the_grants_of_a_table_in_the_trash.py.
About 80 test files moved to uuid objects; tests whose claim is gone (carried grants, stale-on-create,
the rename-register carve-out, truncation flags) were deleted.
